messages:
ana_support: FYI customer (ACME) opened a ticket — their Redwood Private control plane connections started failing after they pushed egress rules yesterday. They see repeated `tls: handshake failure` from their client and our control plane logs show `client hello timed out`. Can someone triage? :thinking:

raj_engineering: On it. Do we have their control plane hostname + an example timestamp? Also, did they move to an outbound proxy/NGFW recently? Those often break mTLS.

acme_netadmin: Hi — thanks. Control plane host is `cp-us-west.redwood-private.acme.internal` (resolves to 10.11.12.34 via their egress NAT). First failing attempt is at 2026-03-15T09:32:11Z. We only changed egress rules to lock down destinations to a small allowlist. No other changes.

marta_eng-sre: Quick checklist: 1) confirm DNS resolves to the expected IP from their egress path, 2) confirm no TLS intercepting proxy rewrites client hello / drops client certs, 3) capture a packet trace and output of `openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -tls1_2 -tlsextdebug -status -servername <host> -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem` so we can see if client sends cert.

john_infra_oncall: Also ask them to run curl debug with client cert to show what the client sees: `curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key --cacert ca.pem https://cp-us-west.redwood-private.acme.internal/health` — paste output. If the proxy is doing TLS MITM, curl will show a different cert chain (issuer mismatch).

acme_netadmin: Pasting their `openssl s_client` run (sanitized):
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.11.12.34:443 -servername cp-us-west.redwood-private.acme.internal -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -tls1_2 -tlsextdebug
CONNECTED(00000003)
140735209345104:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert unknown ca:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1544:SSL alert number 48
---
no peer certificate
---
SSL handshake has read 123 bytes and written 456 bytes
---
Verify return code: 20 (unable to get local issuer certificate)
```

raj_engineering: That `no peer certificate` + verify code 20 suggests the TCP connection completed but the client didn't get a server cert chain that matches the CA they have, or an inline proxy replaced the cert. Also the server didn't request/accept the client cert (or it was stripped). Two likely scenarios: 1) egress proxy terminated TLS and re-initiated a new TLS to our control plane without forwarding client cert info, 2) SNI or hostname mismatch so the control plane returned a default cert the client doesn't trust.

marta_eng-sre: Ask them to capture a packet trace on their egress border while reproducing (tcpdump -s0 -w /tmp/cp-mtls.pcap host 10.11.12.34 and port 443). We need to confirm whether the TLS ClientHello leaves their network unmodified and whether a Client Certificate is ever sent. Check for `CertificateRequest` from server and `Certificate` from client in the TLS handshake. If a middlebox terminates, you'll see two separate TLS sessions (client->proxy and proxy->server).

ana_support (typo corrected): @acme_netadmin also send the exact curl stderr. A lot of customers forget to include `--cacert` and curl will fail with the corporate proxy cert.

acme_netadmin: Here's the curl -v output (sanitized):
```
* About to connect() to 10.11.12.34 port 443 (#0)
*   Trying 10.11.12.34... connected.
* Connected to 10.11.12.34 (10.11.12.34) port 443 (#0)
* found 1 certificates in /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt
* ALPN, server accepted to use h2
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS header, Certificate Status (22):
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2):
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11):
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server key exchange (12):
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server finished (14):
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client key exchange (16):
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Certificate verify (15):
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client finished (16):
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS alert, unknown CA
* SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.corp.local' does not match target host name 'cp-us-west.redwood-private.acme.internal'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL: certificate subject name 'proxy.corp.local' does not match target host name 'cp-us-west.redwood-private.acme.internal'
```

raj_engineering: That output makes it clear: there is a TLS-terminating proxy presenting `proxy.corp.local`. The proxy is not forwarding the client cert — it's terminating TLS. For mTLS to work, the client needs to establish a direct TLS session with our control plane where the server requests a client certificate. With a terminator in the middle, client cert won't be presented to our server (and our logs show missing client cert).

marta_eng-sre: Two remediation options for customer: 1) bypass the TLS-terminating proxy for our control plane host (add to egress allowlist as passthrough), ensure SNI-based passthrough or TCP-level allowlist; 2) configure the proxy to support TLS passthrough for that FQDN / destination IP so client->server mTLS is end-to-end. If their proxy supports `CONNECT` tunneling and no MITM, that works.

john_infra_oncall: I'll add our recommended IP ranges and FQDNs to the ticket and mark as high priority. Also include instructions for verifying end-to-end: run `openssl s_client` from above and confirm you see `CertificateRequest` from server and then `Certificate` from client. A good successful snippet looks like:
```
---
SSL handshake has read 3456 bytes and written 1024 bytes
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/OU=Redwood/CN=cp-us-west.redwood-private.acme.internal
---
Server certificate
---
Verify return code: 0 (ok)
```

ana_support: @acme_netadmin can you confirm if your egress allowlist is hostname-only (some proxies do TLS inspection when only IPs are allowed) or if it's using IP-level passthrough? Also did you recently rotate a corporate root CA?

acme_netadmin: We were told to lock down to explicit IPs yesterday, so likely the proxy intercepted and reissued certs. We'll try switching to hostname passthrough for the control plane and re-test. We'll share pcap + curl/openssl outputs after. Thanks for the quick triage. :pray:

raj_engineering: Thanks — once we have the pcap we can verify whether the `Certificate` from client ever reaches our host. If it doesn't, the issue is on their side (proxy). If it does, we'll look deeper at cipher suite/ALPN mismatches or KMS issues.

deploy-bot: Incident 2026-03-15-ACME-MTLS recorded and linked to ticket #4521.

marta_eng-sre: One more gotcha — if the proxy rewrites SNI to a short name or IP, our control plane selects the wrong serving cert and may not request client cert. Ask them to confirm SNI in the ClientHello (tcpdump shows TLS Client Hello with `Server Name:` extension).

acme_netadmin: Understood, will run the tests and update the ticket in ~30m.

ana_support: Great — we'll stay on standby. :thumbsup:
